title: Air India and Saudia Deepen Partnership With New MOU Beyond Codeshare
excerpt: The two airlines expand their cooperation to include terminal co-location, loyalty programmes, and potential collaboration between flyadeal and Air India Express.
body:
• Air India and Saudia signed a new MOU on July 23 in Gurugram to expand their strategic partnership beyond the existing codeshare agreement.
  • The deal covers expanded codeshare routes, terminal co-location, loyalty programme integration, and potential cooperation between flyadeal and Air India Express.
  • Air India now maintains 25 codeshare partnerships and over 120 interline agreements, providing access to more than 1,000 destinations worldwide.
  • The partnership deepens connectivity for the roughly 2.6 million Indians living in Saudi Arabia, the largest expatriate community in the kingdom.

Air India and Saudia have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to deepen their strategic aviation partnership, expanding cooperation well beyond their existing codeshare arrangement to include terminal co-location, loyalty programmes, and potential collaboration between their low-cost subsidiaries.

The MOU was signed in Gurugram on July 23 by H.E. Engr. Ibrahim Al-Omar, Director General of Saudia Group, and Campbell Wilson, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director of Air India, according to Travel and Tour World.

Beyond Codeshare: A Wider Framework

The two airlines launched their codeshare agreement in February, giving Air India passengers seamless connections via Jeddah and Riyadh to Dammam, Abha, Gassim, Gizan, Madinah, and Taif. Saudia passengers gained access to Indian cities including Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Kolkata, Kochi, Hyderabad, Chennai, Lucknow, and Jaipur via Mumbai and Delhi.

The new MOU goes further, outlining a phased strategy to strengthen codeshare operations, improve network connectivity, evaluate terminal co-location opportunities, and explore loyalty programme cooperation between the two carriers.

Low-Cost Carriers in the Mix

One of the most significant elements of the agreement is the exploration of cooperation between the airlines' subsidiary brands — flyadeal on the Saudia side and Air India Express on the Indian side. This could substantially broaden affordable travel options for budget-conscious travellers between South Asia and the Middle East.

"Saudi Arabia is amongst our most important markets in the Middle East, with the country fast transforming into a major international gateway to the region."

— Campbell Wilson, CEO, Air India

Since its privatisation in 2022, Air India has built 25 codeshare partnerships and more than 120 interline agreements, providing access to over 1,000 destinations worldwide, according to the airline.

Meeting Rising Demand

India and Saudi Arabia continue to experience rising passenger traffic, driven by business ties, family connections, religious journeys, and expanding tourism. Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 programme has opened the kingdom to international tourists, with e-visas and visa-on-arrival now available for eligible Indian passport holders.

Ibrahim Al-Omar noted that Saudia's presence in India spans over 60 years. "It has never been easier to visit the Kingdom," he said, referencing the streamlined visa processes.

Diaspora Connectivity

The expanded partnership holds particular significance for the roughly 2.6 million Indians living in Saudi Arabia — the largest expatriate community in the kingdom. Many travel frequently between the two countries for work, family visits, and religious pilgrimages. Smoother connections, baggage check-through on a single itinerary, and potential loyalty programme integration directly address the needs of this community.

The agreement also comes as Air India separately signed an initial codeshare pact with Riyadh Air, Saudi Arabia's new national carrier, in June, signalling the growing strategic importance of the India-Saudi aviation corridor.
